thesis: Mohnish Pabrai argues that successful entrepreneurs and investors often minimize downside risk rather than taking on high risk, a strategy he describes as 'heads I win, tails I don't lose much.' He illustrates this approach using the examples of a barber expanding into a new town with limited capital and the Patel family, who became low-cost motel operators by employing their own families to avoid payroll costs, thereby achieving high occupancy and supernormal profits.
